newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing says progress made with EU in merger talks.
newsitem.headline: Boeing says progress made with EU in merger talks.

text.p: Progress was made in weekend talks with the European Commission on Boeing's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas, a senior Boeing executive told Reuters on Monday.
"We have not reached a final agreement...we are not there yet," James Frank, Boeing European executive vice president for government and public affairs, said. "We made progress."

"We still are optimistic that we will find a mutually acceptable solution," Frank said. He said the weekend talks had been with the Commission's merger task force, and that Boeing hoped they would continue, but gave no details.

He declined to say whether Boeing had offered further concessions in order to win European Union approval for the $14 billion merger, which has already been cleared by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
EU Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert has made clear the deal could not be approved without Boeing offering "structural" changes to address EU antitrust concerns.
The Commission is due to decide on July 23 whether to approve the merger.
